data.narrative:
Destinus is a late-stage Defense & Security company that has raised $400M+. The broader Defense & Security sector comprises 10 identified comparables (2 public, 8 private), including peers such as Anduril Industries, Helsing, Shield AI, Saronic, and Quantum-Systems.

Valuation was approached using stage-progression analysis, the only applicable triangulation method given data constraints. This method applies a 1.2x step-up multiplier typical of late-stage progression to the $400M total-raised proxy, yielding an implied valuation of $480M. Peer-median analysis was not executable; while 23 same-sector peers exist, none of the filtered subsets (same-stage, adjacent-stage, or similar-tier) contained three or more datapoints necessary for robust median estimation. Applying an all-sector median would introduce material bias.

The analysis supports a valuation range of $408M to $552M, with a median point of $480M. This range reflects ±15% variance around the stage-progression central estimate. Key uncertainties include the representativeness of the $400M raised figure as a current-value proxy—especially given late-stage capital dynamics and the absence of recent transaction or fundraising events. The lack of narrow-set peer multiples limits calibration against Defense & Security-specific revenue or capital efficiency metrics. Additional disclosed transaction data or fundraising events would materially refine this estimate.
